title: introduce-needle-sampler-and-token-cost-correlator-with-backchain-index
author: Anika Rao
release_notes: Adds a low-overhead "needle" sampling mode that prioritizes rare token sequences and long-tail kernel backtraces; introduces a compact trace backchain index and dashboard panels for correlating token-level cost with kernel execution paths; rollout behind feature flag; non-breaking.
description:
Context: Long-tail token/sequence shapes cause disproportionate cost and SLO churn but are rare, so sampling needs to be both precise and cheap. This PR implements a lightweight 'needle' sampler that: 1) continuously scores incoming invocations by sequence-shape rarity and observed per-token cost, 2) escalates sampling probability for invocations with anomalous kernel latency patterns, and 3) records a compact backchain representation (kernel-ID -> queued-duration -> phase-breakdown) to a new trace index. Goal: improve signal-to-noise for operators and SREs while keeping telemetry egress and query costs low.

What this PR does (single-pass summary): Adds a new sampling pipeline (redwood/observability/needle_sampler.rs) with a pluggable scoring function, a compact on-disk backchain indexer (redwood/observability/trace_index/compact_indexer.py) that stores backchains as deduplicated shards, a token-cost correlator service (redwood/telemetry/token_cost_correlator.py) that joins sampled traces with token-cost rollups, and dashboard panels (telemetry/dashboards/needle_sampling.panel.json) to visualize sequence-shape index, sampled backchains, and top-correlated kernels. Also updates the Python SDK telemetry hooks (sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py) to expose the lightweight sampling header and a feature-flag gating mechanism.

Design notes: - Needle sampler design chooses ~0.1% baseline sampling and applies multiplicative boosts for rare sequence-shapes (low-frequency n-gram fingerprint) and multi-phase kernel stalls. The scoring function is configurable via runtime flags and tuned to avoid skewing production SLOs. - Backchain index is intentionally compact: we store a shingled lineage of kernel IDs + phase durations (at 1ms resolution) instead of full spans to reduce storage and query costs. Reconstruction code can hydrate the full span when needed. - Correlator computes Spearman correlations between per-token cost vectors and kernel-phase latencies across sampled population and produces ranked kernel suspects for pull-through investigation.

Rollout plan: Feature-flagged under telemetry.experimental.needle_sampling. Start in staging for 48h synthetic replay, then opt-in to 5% production traffic for 72h with perf counters monitored. If CPU/ingest cost exceeds budget, the default sampling rate will be cut in half. Full rollout requires a follow-up migration doc to add long-term retention policy for the compact index.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the score function and indexer included; an integration test (tests/integration/test_needle_sampling.py) replays historical traces and validates backchain reconstruction fidelity. Load test in perf-lab shows sampling adds <0.6% p99 latency and ~3% telemetry ingest increase at 5% traffic. CI: one flaky e2e in SDK telemetry hook was fixed in an additional commit.

Operational impacts and runbook: - New telemetry metric: telemetry.needle.sampled_invocations (counter) and telemetry.needle.correlator_jobs (gauge). - Add an alert: needle-sampler-ingest-surge if sampled_invocations > expected_rate * 1.8 for 30m. - Dashboard includes an "Investigate" link that opens a compact backchain viewer and pre-populates a kernel suspect list.

Related work: ENG-2984 (observability long-tail projects), SUP-1123 (customer incident pointing to kernel phase stalls).
commit_summary: Initial needle sampler pipeline and scoring function (observability/needle_sampler.rs)
Compact backchain indexer and hydration helpers (observability/trace_index/compact_indexer.py)
Token-cost correlator service and dashboard panels (telemetry/token_cost_correlator.py, telemetry/dashboards/needle_sampling.panel.json)
SDK hook + feature flag gating and tests (sdk/python/redwood/telemetry.py, tests/integration/test_needle_sampling.py)
Fix flaky SDK telemetry e2e test (tests/e2e/fix-telemetry-hook)
discussion: Marco Li: Nice direction — can we make the sampling caps configurable per-tenant? I'm worried about multitenant hotspots.
Anika Rao (author): Good point; added tenant_cap argument and a default 10x cap in the config. See compact_indexer.py config block.
Priya Singh: Please add a feature-flag kill switch in the feature rollout section and ensure the dashboard panels gracefully handle zero data.
Anika Rao (author): Added telemetry.experimental.needle_sampling.disable flag and panel fallbacks. Also added unit test for empty-index rendering.
James O'Neill: The correlator's Spearman computation could be expensive at scale; suggest a streaming approximate quantile join instead of full-sort grouping.
Anika Rao (author): Swapped to an incremental rank-approximation with reservoir sketching for large cohorts (see token_cost_correlator.py commit). Reduced memory by ~40% in perf tests.
QA (Sophie Tan): Integration tests passed in staging; ran a 48h synthetic replay, no SLO violations observed.
Ops (Ravi Patel): Approved rollout. Added runbook snippet under docs/observability/needle_sampling.md.
notes_for_release: Feature gated; enable via telemetry.experimental.needle_sampling. Default off. See docs/observability/needle_sampling.md for rollout and runbook.
